reading.body:
Profit Finder Pro Software is not a data center. It is a customer relationship management and sales-tracking product for roofing, solar, contracting, and insurance trades, mistagged in OpenStreetMap as telecom=data_center at a Scottsdale address now occupied by another company.

The entry carries no capacity figure, no operator, and no published specifications. Its stored coordinates resolve to TraVek Inc at 15575 North 83rd Way, Scottsdale, a different current occupant, and nothing publicly available connects either the software business or that address to server infrastructure or colocation equipment. The address also sits several miles from the other eight rows in the same batch, so no single shared building links them. Each is an independently mistagged small business scattered across the Phoenix metro.

This matters for AI infrastructure accounting because facility lists are the input to capacity and grid-load estimates. A phantom point with zero megawatts does not inflate Arizona's total, which stands at 512 MW across four facilities with published figures, but it shows how a land-use or telecom tag can enter a dataset as a building that consumes power. Cleaning that class of error is cheap. Leaving it in makes every downstream count less trustworthy.

What this does not establish is how many other mistagged points exist, or anything about the four Arizona facilities that do publish capacity. It covers one address, one software company, and one exhausted line of research.
